sources: Miro — journey alignment board (design sprint, what the team landed on)

prototype.note: Each stage lists the prototype views and JS hooks that cover it, so this spec can drive a guided-tour / scenario mode inside the prototype.

coverageScale.missing: Not in this prototype (may exist in another file)

personas.name: Bob Iversen
personas.summary: Existing customer, all data connected. Sees verified figures from day one; his journey starts at stage 3–4 on most visits.

personas.name: Fanny Kristensen
personas.summary: New customer, no data yet. Lands on peer-benchmark estimates (electrical contracting, 148 peers) — the anti-cold-start strategy. Stages 1–3 decide whether she connects data and stays.

stages.title: Log in
stages.userGoal: Get into the portal quickly — driven by a specific need, a notification, or wanting an overview.
doing: Logs into the portal because they have a specific need, received a notification, or want an overview.
stages.thinking: I want to get to the thing that brought me here, not to a generic start page.
systemBehavior: Notifications should deep-link into the relevant view (savings, opportunity, agreement change), not just to the dashboard.

prototype.notes: Prototype login is a persona picker that lands straight on the right dashboard. Real authentication and notification deep-links are out of scope here.

gaps: Notification → deep-link entry path is not demonstrated; every session starts at the dashboard.

personaNotes.bob: Returning with intent — often triggered by a notification.
personaNotes.fanny: First visit; the login promise ('your invoices already know where the money is going') sets expectations.

stages.title: Connect spend data
stages.userGoal: Give the product real data with the least effort and risk, so figures become exact instead of estimated.
doing: Decides whether to connect to the ERP or upload a spend report.
stages.thinking: Is this worth the effort? What do I get if I connect, and what happens to my data?
systemBehavior: If connected to the ERP, the product can notice procurement made outside of agreements and suggest suppliers that fit.
Until data is connected, figures are peer-based estimates and clearly marked as such (estimated vs verified).

prototype.notes: v2-visual still ships the CSS for the dedicated onboarding screens (Sources, Loading/analyzing, Data set confirm, CEO welcome) but their markup was removed — the full connect flow lives in advantage-onboarding.html. Here, connecting is reachable via the Data center only.

gaps: End-to-end connect flow (choose source → analyze → confirm data set → value reveal) is not walkable in this file.
Off-agreement procurement detection (the ERP payoff) is described but not shown.

personaNotes.bob: Skips this stage — data already connected (all figures verified).
personaNotes.fanny: The critical conversion moment: estimates must be compelling enough to justify connecting.

stages.title: Understand current position
stages.userGoal: See my procurement situation at a glance — agreements, suppliers, spend — without doing analysis myself.
doing: Reviews the company's current agreements, suppliers, purchasing spend and overall procurement situation.
stages.thinking: Does this picture match reality? Can I trust these numbers?
systemBehavior: Present what similar companies are doing based on AI analysis, so new customers never see a cold, empty start.
First login shows a one-time explainer for estimated vs verified data before a benchmark number can be mistaken for a real one.

prototype.notes: The anti-cold-start decision from the sprint is implemented: Fanny lands on peer-based estimates for her industry and size.

personaNotes.bob: Verified agreements, suppliers and spend from his own invoices.
personaNotes.fanny: Everything is an estimate from her peer group — dashed/estimated styling carries the honesty.

stages.title: See realized & potential value
stages.userGoal: Understand what Advantage has already saved me and what's still on the table.
doing: Uses the Savings Dashboard to understand realized savings, potential savings, spend through agreements and accumulated customer bonus.
Reviews notifications about new savings opportunities, agreement changes, achieved savings or decisions requiring attention.
stages.thinking: This is what the service is worth to us. What needs my attention?
systemBehavior: Realized vs potential is always shown as one story (the sketches' '7 mil NOK' reveal).
Notifications are relevance-filtered: new opportunities, agreement changes, achieved savings, decisions pending.

prototype.notes: Realized, potential, spend-through-agreements and customer bonus are all present.

personaNotes.bob: Peak moment of the journey — verified realized savings plus bonus.
personaNotes.fanny: Sees potential only; the number is the argument for connecting data.

stages.title: Discover opportunity
stages.userGoal: Find where we can cut costs or get better terms — without hunting for it.
doing: Sees proactively identified categories where the company could reduce costs, improve terms or move more spend to Advantage agreements.
Uses the AI Procurement Agent to understand opportunities, ask questions and identify where to focus next.
stages.thinking: Which of these is worth my limited time?
systemBehavior: Opportunities are proactively surfaced and ranked, not searched for.
The agent answers 'where should we focus next?' with reasons grounded in the company's own data.

prototype.notes: Both discovery modes from the Miro board (proactive categories + conversational agent) are in the prototype.

personaNotes.bob: Weekly discovery cadence — findings since Monday.
personaNotes.fanny: 'Easy first win' framing (widest rate gap in her trade) lowers the entry bar.

stages.title: Review business case
stages.userGoal: See the concrete case for one opportunity: what we spend, what we'd save, and why this is relevant to us.
doing: Reviews potential savings, current spend, recommended agreement, expected value and why the opportunity is relevant.
stages.thinking: Show me the numbers and the reasoning — is this credible?
systemBehavior: Every recommendation explains 'why relevant' — grounded in the company's spend, not generic.
Method and timeline are available but folded away once read, keeping the saving and agreements in front.

screens.name: Business case dialog (e.g. 1.2 mil NOK / yr)

prototype.notes: Matches the sketches' business-case card ('1.2 mil NOK / yr' → 'Ready to decide?').

personaNotes.fanny: Case built on estimates — needs the estimated-marking to stay honest here too.

stages.title: Evaluate
stages.userGoal: Judge whether switching supplier or agreement actually makes business sense for us.
doing: Assesses whether changing supplier or agreement makes business sense based on savings, terms, risk, effort and other business considerations.
stages.thinking: Savings are one thing — what about terms, switching effort, delivery risk, existing relationships?
systemBehavior: The agent should answer evaluation questions (terms, risk, effort) — not only savings math.

prototype.notes: Savings and method are covered; the broader business considerations are only reachable by asking the agent.

gaps: No explicit terms / risk / switching-effort comparison in the business case — the Miro board names these as decision inputs.
No side-by-side of current agreement vs recommended agreement.

personaNotes.bob: May involve colleagues — the case needs to be shareable/exportable eventually.
personaNotes.fanny: Evaluation doubles as evaluation of Advantage itself.

stages.title: Decide
stages.userGoal: Commit with an appropriate level of effort: proceed, get an offer, approve the switch — or hand it to an advisor.
doing: Decides whether to proceed with the opportunity, request an offer, approve a switch or involve an Advantage advisor.
stages.thinking: What exactly happens when I press this? Can I undo it? Who does the work?
systemBehavior: Every decision path is low-risk framed: requesting an offer or involving an advisor commits to nothing.
Decisions requiring attention resurface via notifications (stage 4) if parked.

prototype.notes: CTAs and advisor path exist; what happens after the click is not shown.

gaps: No post-decision state: confirmation, expected next steps, status tracking of a requested offer or switch.
No visible distinction in commitment level between 'request offer' and 'approve switch'.

personaNotes.bob: Wants self-serve approval with a clear undo window.
personaNotes.fanny: First decision will likely go through the advisor — that path builds trust.

stages.title: Prove value
stages.userGoal: Show (to myself and internally) that the decisions paid off — and stay compliant while doing it.
doing: Sees accumulated and paid customer bonus as an additional part of the value generated through the agreements.
Accesses relevant supplier and compliance documentation when needed, including documentation related to the Transparency Act.
stages.thinking: I can defend this internally: here's what we saved, here's the bonus, here's the paperwork.
systemBehavior: Bonus is presented as accumulated and paid — value beyond the price savings.
Compliance documentation (incl. Transparency Act / Åpenhetsloven) is retrievable per supplier when needed.

prototype.notes: Bonus is in the savings dashboard; documentation is not in this prototype (Reports nav item is a stub).

gaps: Supplier & compliance documentation (Transparency Act) has no screen anywhere in v2-visual.
No export/share of the value story for internal reporting.

personaNotes.bob: Uses bonus + realized savings as the renewal argument.
personaNotes.fanny: Her first registered saving is the moment the estimates become real.

stages.title: Prioritize next opportunity
stages.userGoal: Let results and recommendations tell me what to optimize next — keep the loop going without effort.
doing: Uses realized results and AI recommendations to decide which purchasing category or agreement to optimize next.
stages.thinking: That worked — what's next? Keep them coming.
systemBehavior: The customer gets notified when new suppliers matching their spending data are added.
The customer is notified when savings potential is registered that isn't being utilized.

prototype.notes: The ingredients exist; the loop (this realized result → therefore this next recommendation) is not made explicit.

gaps: New-supplier-match and unused-potential notifications are named on the board but not simulated.
Recommendations don't visibly reference realized results ('office supplies saved 19% — flooring shows the same pattern').

personaNotes.bob: This stage closes his loop back to stage 4/5 on the next visit.
personaNotes.fanny: Once here, she has become Bob.
